title: Introduction to Logic and to the Methodology of Deductive Sciences
byline: Alfred Tarski · Oxford University Press (English edition)
note: Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: Tarski’s classic introduction for readers without mathematical training. The first part teaches elementary logic as the language of mathematics: variables and quantifiers, the sentential calculus with truth tables and laws of inference, identity, the calculus of classes, and relations (including functions and order), then explains the deductive method itself: primitive terms, axioms, definitions, proofs, models, consistency, completeness and independence. The second part applies all of this by axiomatizing a small theory of order and addition for numbers, examining its methodological properties, and extending it toward the real numbers.
